variants.headline: Household savings committed to a company plan
variants.sub: Household savings have been put into a business plan by {founder}.
variants.body:
The settler {founder} has put household savings into a plan for {business} in {district}. The commitment is a plan to start a company, not an announcement that it has opened. For {target}, the relevant question concerns the conditions under which a household commits its means to an undertaking.

A plan backed by savings is a commitment, not an operating business. Our assessment favours {target} over a verdict that confuses an adverse interpretation with an established fact.

variants.headline: An enterprise begins as a household risk
variants.sub: The founder {founder} has backed a plan for {business} with household savings.
variants.body:
Household savings are behind the plan made by {founder} for {business} in {district}. A future company is the intention, rather than an established operation. Readers assessing {target} should keep the person and household behind that intention in view, alongside the practical difference between planning and opening.

A plan backed by savings is a commitment, not an operating business. Our assessment favours {target} over a verdict that confuses an adverse interpretation with an established fact.

variants.headline: A settler backs a business idea
variants.sub: The settler {founder} has committed household savings to a plan for {business}.
variants.body:
The founder {founder} has backed a plan for {business} in {district} with household savings. There is a personal commitment within the commercial proposal. Any reckoning with {target} should distinguish respect for that commitment from a promise that the enterprise will open or produce a particular result.

A plan backed by savings is a commitment, not an operating business. Our assessment favours {target} over a verdict that confuses an adverse interpretation with an established fact.
